sample_unit: virtual patients with type 1 diabetes (in silico trial)
models_evaluated: three offline reinforcement learning algorithms (unnamed in the abstract)

links.outcome: Gap between retrospective evaluation on resampled data and returns when agents were deployed in the simulator
links.effect: Retrospective evaluation on resampled data predicted 1.5-3x better returns than agents achieved in practice. Temporal resampling reduced performance by up to 60%, and 4-hour binning left all agents worse than the dataset baseline.
links.quote: Retrospective evaluation on resampled data actively obscured this effect, predicting 1.5-3x better returns than agents achieved in practice.

unlisted_practices: Train offline reinforcement learning on datasets with natural clinical timings between decisions rather than temporally resampled (binned) data

screen.reason: Evaluates how data preprocessing (temporal binning/resampling vs preserving natural clinical timing) impacts safety and policy performance of offline reinforcement learning agents in a simulated clinical trial.

primary.practice: avoiding temporal resampling/binning in offline training data
